procedure.description: breast reconstruction, immediate or delayed, with tissue expander

denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 19357 (breast reconstruction, immediate or delayed, with tissue expander) with date of service 2026-05-28. CARC 197: Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent. Payer remark: No authorization is on file. A retrospective medical necessity review may be requested with supporting clinical documentation within 180 days.

criteria.text: Documented mastectomy for breast cancer, or prophylactic mastectomy for a qualifying risk, with reconstruction requested by the patient. Reconstruction after a covered mastectomy is a mandated benefit under the Women’s Health and Cancer Rights Act.
An operative plan for staged reconstruction (tissue expander placement followed by implant exchange) appropriate to the patient’s radiation status and tissue quality.
Medical clearance for the planned surgery is documented.

chart.text: Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance. From the breast surgeon: left total mastectomy performed 4 months ago for a 2.3 centimeter invasive ductal carcinoma, sentinel nodes negative, margins clear. She has completed adjuvant chemotherapy and wishes to proceed with reconstruction.

44 year old woman referred by the breast surgeon for reconstruction. Went over expanders versus flaps, she prefers the expander route, fewer operations and no donor site. Her history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, reflux on omeprazole as needed. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Status post left mastectomy 4 months ago for a 2.3 centimeter invasive ductal. Done with chemo. She wants reconstruction and has thought hard about it. No radiation planned per oncology. Good skin envelope, no infection, mastectomy flap healed. Plan is a left tissue expander under the pectoralis now, exchange to a permanent implant in about 6 months, and a right lift for symmetry later.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 188, LDL 124, HDL 38, triglycerides 189. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Blood pressure check. 144 over 90 today, 124 over 87 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Back with her sister to go over the plan again. Questions answered. Ready to schedule. Vitals today 136 over 75, pulse 62.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
A1c came back 6.6. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Called to let her know the surgery date is set and that we are submitting to the insurance. She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.4, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Pre-op. Cleared by her PCP, letter in the chart, labs and EKG fine. Consent signed for left tissue expander placement.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 197 denial can be answered from the record.
